newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt and Turkey ask Israel to close tunnel. [CORRECTED 13:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt and Turkey ask Israel to close tunnel. [CORRECTED 13:25 GMT]

text.p: Egypt and Turkey issued a joint call on Friday for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to close the controversial Jerusalem tunnel entrance that has sparked a crisis in Middle East peace talks.

Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri issued the statement at a ceremony in which the two countries -- both with full relations with Israel -- signed a number of bilateral agreements.

"The two prime ministers...expressed their concerns about the events in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza resulting from the opening of the tunnel under al-Aqsa mosque by Israeli authorities. They called on the Israeli government to close the tunnel immediately and not to resort to force," it said.

Since Netanyahu ordered the opening of an entrance to the tunnel in the Moslem quarter of Jerusalem's Old City near Islam's third holiest site, 58 Arabs and 15 Israelis (Corrects from 16 Israelis) have died in clashes.
Despite international appeals for Netanyahu to close the tunnel, which previous Israeli governments had opted not to open, Netanyahu has said it will stay open forever.

A summit in Washington this week failed to narrow differences on any major issue between Israelis and Palestinians but peace talks are resuming on Sunday in Israel, focused on getting Israel to carry out its promised redeployment of troops in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron .

"The two sides called on the Israeli government to take full responsibilities for agreements reached between Israel and Palestine, to renew without delay and with good intention peace talks in line with the Madrid recommendations and to refrain from any action which threatens the peace talks, including changes in the status of Jerusalem and settlements," it added.

Erbakan is the first Islamist prime minister of the Turkish republic but has not cancelled military agreements reached this year with Israel before he took office. Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab country to reach a peace treaty with Israel,
